title: Declarative canary policy engine with traffic splits and guardrails
creator: Marco Chen
description: Goal: Ship a declarative, policy-driven canary rollout engine for model versions that supports traffic splits, step schedules, shadow traffic, A/B test variants, safety guardrails, and automatic rollback. The engine should be exposed via the Redwood Console and API, integrate with observability (per-route dashboards, tracing hooks) and the serving runtime to enforce traffic routing and fallbacks. Key behaviors: 1) Declarative rollout spec (YAML/JSON) describing steps, traffic percentages, windows, evaluation metrics, and rollback triggers. 2) Support phased canaries, percentage-based A/B variants, and optional shadow routing for offline evaluation. 3) Guardrails: latency p95, error rate, cost per token delta, and quality regressions measured by eval prompt set; thresholds trigger pause/rollback. 4) Auto-rollback policy with configurable grace periods and automated rollback reasons recorded to audit logs. 5) Compatibility with Dedicated and Private deployments: policy enforcement must be local to control plane when required. 6) Auditability and RBAC: every step change requires actor + reason; rollbacks surface in Console timeline.
notes: 2026-02-20 — Initial PRD drafted by Marco. Outlines DSL for rollout specs and metric evaluation. Links to benchmarking notes and initial UX sketches.

2026-02-25 — Spike complete: ran a toy implementation that enforces 10% -> 50% traffic steps and triggers rollback on p95>1200ms. Results: runtime hook latency added ~5ms per request under heavy load. Recorded in /docs/spikes/canary-spike-02-25.md.

2026-03-02 — Design review with UX (Rina) and PM (Jules). Agreed to show step timeline, metric overlays, and explicit "Approve" button for manual progression in Console. Action: Aisha to prototype timeline widget.

2026-03-08 — Implementation kickoff. Core components: rollout coordinator service (state machine), evaluator (pulls metrics from metrics pipeline), and router integration (config push to serving runtime). Assigned tasks split across infra and runtime teams.
open_todos: Finalize rollout DSL: support 'canary', 'ab_test', 'shadow' types and allow custom metric expressions
Define evaluation metric set and default thresholds (p95_latency, error_rate_5m, model_quality_delta@eval-set)
Design Console timeline and API schema for submissions and manual approvals
Add end-to-end tests: simulated traffic, metric injection, and rollback scenarios
Coordinate Dedicated/Private deployment plan for control-plane optionality
decisions: Use declarative rollout specs stored in project config; persisted in DB with immutable revision IDs
Evaluation will be both windowed (sliding) and step-end aggregated; default window = 5m but configurable per-step
Auto-rollback will be enabled by default for P0 customers but configurable per-deployment
Router integration will be a config push with versioned traffic tables rather than per-request proxying to minimize latency impact
blockers: Metrics pipeline needs a low-latency path for per-route p95 aggregation (ENG-5180)
Clarify compliance requirements for audit log retention in Private deployments (security team)
acceptance_criteria: Create rollout spec API that accepts YAML/JSON and returns a rollout_id
Coordinator enforces step schedule and pushes traffic configuration to runtime with zero downtime
Evaluator triggers pause/rollback when thresholds are breached and records a detailed rollback reason
Console displays live rollout state, metric overlays, and supports manual step approval
E2E tests validate canary -> full rollout path and at least two rollback scenarios
